scripts.radio:
Habari zenu, this is Kenyans Are Asking.

This week, three numbers demand our attention: 10.5 trillion, seven years, and 6.3 million.

First, Kenya’s public debt has breached 10.5 trillion shillings. Parliament is finally talking about setting up an open register. Why did it take this long? When debt is contracted behind closed doors, ordinary citizens pay for it in broad daylight through punishing taxes. We must insist on a transparent ledger showing every lender, every interest rate, and every stalled project.

Second, Senator Samson Cherargei is reviving his bid to extend the presidential term from five to seven years. Let us be plain: sovereign power belongs to the people under Article 1. Tinkering with constitutional term limits while citizens struggle with basic survival shows political priorities that are completely out of touch.

Finally, the IEBC plans to register 6.3 million new voters ahead of 2027. But how does that happen when thousands of young Kenyans cannot get national IDs? Processing bottlenecks at Huduma centres are locking out the next generation. If the state cannot print IDs on time, it compromises the integrity of the next election before it even starts.

Kwa ufupi: Deni la taifa limevuka trilioni kumi nukta tano, na bunge lazima liweke wazi kila senti. Wakati huo huo, mpango wa kuongeza muhula wa rais hadi miaka saba hauna mashiko huku vijana wakinyimwa vitambulisho vya kupiga kura. Simama imara, uliza maswali, na usikubali kupotoshwa.
scripts.voice_note:
Jambo fam, here is your weekly briefing from Kenyans Are Asking.

Watch the political sleight of hand happening right now. Senator Cherargei is back with that proposal to stretch the presidential term limit from five to seven years. Kenyans already said no to this, and sovereign power rests with citizens, not politicians looking to secure longer tenures.

Meanwhile, the IEBC wants to register 6.3 million new voters for 2027, but national ID processing is practically frozen in several sub-counties. If young people cannot get IDs, they cannot register to vote. That is disenfranchisement through bureaucratic neglect.

Add to that our public debt passing 10.5 trillion shillings, with Parliament only now waking up to push for an open register.

Do not let constitutional sideshows distract you from service delivery and governance failures. Check on your ID status, follow the debt register debate, and pass this note along.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe tip: Getting your national ID is a constitutional right, not a favor. Don't let bureaucratic delays lock you out of voting in 2027. Demand it early.
scripts.reels: Five years isn't too short; it is a constitutional contract. Yet Senator Samson Cherargei is back, pushing to extend the presidential term limit to seven years. When Kenyans are battling high taxes, unemployment, and rising debt, whose priority is keeping politicians in power longer? Article 1 says sovereign power belongs to the people, not leaders rewriting terms to suit themselves. We don't need longer terms. We need accountable leadership.
